subject: Trial economics & credit guardrails — Acme Health pilot
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Susan Wu <susan.wu@acmehealth.com>, Tom Price <tom.price@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-07T13:15:00-07:00
Subject: ACME pilot — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Susan / Tom,

Thanks again for taking time today — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up the pilot: 

Key takeaways from discovery:
- Primary workload: conversational assistant + summarization for clinical notes (approx 70% gen, 30% embeddings).
- Expected daily active users (DAU): 150–250 during pilot; peak concurrency 8–12.
- Average prompt + response length: ~500 tokens round-trip.
- Goal: validate quality and infra costs; target unit economics (rule of thumb) ~$800–$1,200 per 1M tokens depending on quantization and batching.

Pilot proposal (30-day):
1) Redwood will provision a pilot tenant and provide initial credits to cover ~50k–60k tokens/day (see cost note below).
2) Mutual Action Plan attached (acme-mutual-action-plan.xlsx) — please review timeline and owners.
3) We’ll instrument token-level telemetry and a weekly burn-rate check-in.

Cost and credit guardrails (proposal):
- Baseline credit: 30,000 free credits (~equivalent to our conservative $/1M tokens at 12% discount — details attached).
- Burn-rate safety: if pilot consumes >60% of credits within 10 days, we pause ingestion and set up a sync to discuss scaling or a temporary extension.
- If Acme confirms a target $/1M tokens and commit level, we can propose committed dedicated capacity to hit that unit cost.

Action items:
- Susan: confirm whether procurement needs a PO before we enable the tenant (you mentioned procurement@acmehealth.com).
- Tom: confirm a firm start date for the pilot (we suggested next Monday).
- I’ll follow up with a short cost breakdown PDF and the MAP.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-cheatsheet.pdf, acme-mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes

From: Susan Wu <susan.wu@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Re: ACME pilot — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Camila — that recap is super helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before procurement and our internal stakeholders sign off:

1) Can you spell out the assumed unit economics that produced the $800–$1,200 / 1M tokens range? Specifically: model variant, quantization level, and whether embeddings and generation are priced the same in the pilot.
2) What do you mean by "free credits" — is that $ value or token-equivalent? We need that number for our budget owners.
3) If we hit >60% of credits fast, what is the typical timeline to extend credits or move to a paid trial? We may want a buffer while procurement processes a PO.

Procurement note: procurement@acmehealth.com — we often require a PO before enabling vendor access. If Redwood needs to enable the tenant earlier, we may need a short-term exception.

Can you send the cost calc and a recommended target $/1M tokens for our use-case?

— Susan
Susan Wu
Director, Product Innovation | Acme Health
susan.wu@acmehealth.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Susan Wu <susan.wu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Tom Price <tom.price@acmehealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-08T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME pilot — post-call recap & next steps

Susan — great questions. Below is a concise cost breakdown and the exact assumptions that map to the $/1M tokens range we discussed.

Assumptions used:
- Model: open-llama-v2-like baseline (serving parity with 7B-class for latency); option to switch to quantized 4-bit for cost savings.
- Quantization options: FP16 (best perf, higher cost), 8-bit, 4-bit (lowest cost, slight quality delta).
- Mix: Estimated 70% generation (higher per-token), 30% embeddings (lower per-unit but still charged).

Representative unit economics (pilot-level, hosted inference, US region):
- FP16 baseline: ~$1,200 / 1M tokens
- 8-bit quantized: ~$950 / 1M tokens
- 4-bit quantized + batching: ~$800 / 1M tokens (likely with throughput tuning and prefix caching)

Notes: these are token-cost estimates for the inference portion only (does not include storage or optional dedicated throughput add-ons). We provide further optimizations via Redwood Optimize (suggested batching/cache settings), which typically reduces cost by 10–30% depending on request distribution.

Credits explanation:
- "30,000 free credits" — our internal shorthand for a dollar-equivalent credit that maps to token consumption under the pilot pricing plan. For transparency: 30,000 credits ≈ $3,000 in pilot spend (token equivalent ~3.5–4M tokens depending on the quantization tier chosen). Exact token conversion will be shown in the console.

Extension and guardrail options:
- If the pilot consumes >60% within the first 10 days, we propose a manual pause + a quick sync to decide on either: (a) add an incremental 25k credits as a one-time extension, or (b) fast-track procurement for PO and enable a paid trial.
- Timeline: Rishi can approve up to 25k incremental credits immediately; anything beyond that goes to revenue leadership. Typically we can apply the incremental credits same-day after internal approval.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-cheatsheet.pdf (detailed per-quantization table), acme-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (timeline & owners).

Ask: If that all looks good, please confirm:
- Whether procurement requires a PO before tenant enablement (Y/N).
- Preferred pilot start date (we have slots Monday 2026-06-14 or Wednesday 2026-06-16).
- Preferred quantization target (FP16 / 8-bit / 4-bit) or we can default to 8-bit for first week.

Thanks — Camila
